title: Two-rune feedback with every starting pair
question: Do any two-rune starting keys pass the fixed source-family English-score gates?
reader_question: Can any starting pair make these two-rune feedback rules yield a strong English score?
bounds_note: Seven fixed functions; every two-rune start; page-local English scoring.
summary: No candidate passed the frozen score rules; 35 of 49 shuffled whole-family searches scored at least as highly. Known-input controls also show that the top-scoring output is not always the complete true text.
finding: All 2,590,280 labelled cases (2,220,240 effective cases) were scored. Best is −6.163949899504046 on LP2-51, lastdiff/plaintext/sign −1/forward, starting key [9,16], below absolute −5.5 and the joint −5.330115462503459 gate. Whole-family shuffled maxima >= observed: 35/49. True supplied keys recover in all 336 constructed controls and pass −5.5, but unique truth ranks first in 216, 88 have ties-only and 32 have a strictly higher alternative; earliest-best complete recovery is 264/336. All observed scores match an independent implementation exactly. No cipher-family rejection follows.
reader_finding: No starting pair passed the fixed score checks. Thirty-five of 49 shuffled searches scored at least as highly; some controls ranked a wrong output above the known text.
reader_limit: One fixed two-rune feedback family and English scorer. The controls reuse only two passages; this is score screening, not a validated rejection of autokey ciphers.
limitations: Other history lengths/functions, continuous or word-reset streams, skipping, different alphabets or language scorers, plaintext identification, per-branch significance claims and control-validated cipher-family rejection. Identification controls reuse two passages, three starts and dependent branch labels: all 336 true-key outputs recover, but only 264 selected winners recover completely; 88 ties-only and 32 higher wrong alternatives remain material limits. Null full-grid independent checks are sampled; observed scores and reported null maxima are all independently checked.
next_steps: Use any concrete alternative as a separately frozen proposal. Inspect exact retained outputs and identification failures before interpreting a high English score; do not promote this finite result to a whole-family or language exclusion.

changes.before: For each stream, sweep seven fixed feedback functions, k=2..6, three history sources, both signs and both directions; score decoded transliteration using the pinned English quadgram table and 29 all-equal seeds for plaintext/mixed history.

Repeat the same whole-family selection on 49 shared within-page-shuffled corpora. Retain failed known-text identification diagnostics; interpret as fixed score-screening enumeration only.

review.kind: complete finite source-family score enumeration with independent reconstruction
review.reviewer: Independent direct formulas/raw quadgram scorer check all 2,220,240 observed scores, all 150,920 reported null maxima, sampled 432 fixed full null grids plus 49 winner grids, stable alias selection and 146 full witnesses; 2,312,750 prior-corner scores also match exactly. Identification failures retained.

reproduction.environment: Recorded Python 3.12.10, NumPy 2.5.4 and Numba 0.67.0; pins in requirements.txt. All needed source/model/input files bundled. Scripts install nothing and make no network/model calls. Quick check runs no decoding searches; full replay stages a temporary directory, repeats all original controls plus the entire observed/49-null family, independently checks and compares deterministic values and exact numeric bytes without overwriting expected files.

visuals.caption: Dots summarize the best score from each complete family search. Both frozen score rules remain unmet; known-input ranking sometimes chooses a different output than the complete true text.
